title: Your First Script
description: Write hello.sh with a proper shebang, make it executable and verify its output.
scenario: The team keeps pasting the same boot-check command into terminals by hand. Your lead asks you to turn it into your first script: /home/intern/hello.sh must print exactly 'Opslance boot OK' when run. It needs a proper shebang so it runs under bash no matter who invokes it, and the executable bit so it can be run directly.
symptoms: There is no boot-check script yet — everyone types the command manually
Scripts without a shebang behave differently depending on how they are invoked
A script without the executable bit cannot be run as ./hello.sh
mission: Create /home/intern/hello.sh starting with #!/bin/bash that prints exactly 'Opslance boot OK', make it executable, and run it.

hints.title: The shebang line
hints.content: The first line `#!/bin/bash` tells the kernel which interpreter to use. Without it, ./hello.sh may run under sh with different behaviour.

hints.title: Create and edit
hints.content: Use `nano /home/intern/hello.sh` to write the two lines, or `printf`/`cat` from the shell.

hints.title: The executable bit
hints.content: `chmod +x /home/intern/hello.sh` adds execute permission so `./hello.sh` works, not just `bash hello.sh`.

acceptance_criteria.description: first line of the script is the shebang #!/bin/bash
script has the executable bit set
running the script prints exactly 'Opslance boot OK'
